findings.comment: The jq filter does not match the input format. `files_jsonl` contains one JSON object per line (see the comment: `jq -c '.[]' <<<"$batch" >>"$files_jsonl"`), so jq runs `any(.[]; .patch != null)` once per file object. Even without the error, `any` over one object's values could never answer 'does any file in the batch have a patch?'.
